Species traits, with or without phylogenetic signal

Source: R/traits.R
species_traits.Rd

Environmental optima evolve by Brownian motion with Pagel's lambda and are rescaled to optima_range (or, with uniform_optima = TRUE, replaced by ranks with evenly spaced values on that range, so that only their arrangement on the tree depends on the tree). Niche breadths are drawn from a normal distribution truncated at zero, and maximum growth rates from a uniform distribution. Either can carry phylogenetic signal: the values are then assigned to species by the ranks of a Brownian-motion trait, which keeps their marginal distribution.

Usage

species_traits(
  species,
  lambda = 1,
  optima_range = c(0, 100),
  uniform_optima = FALSE,
  sigma_mean = 10,
  sigma_sd = 10,
  rmax_range = c(2, 8),
  sigma_signal = FALSE,
  rmax_signal = FALSE,
  optima = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  r_max = NULL,
  rescale_optima = TRUE,
  nodes = FALSE
)

Arguments

species

A phylo tree, or the number of species for traits without phylogenetic structure.

lambda

Pagel's lambda of the optima (0 = no signal, 1 = Brownian motion). Ignored when species is a number.

optima_range

Range of the optima.

uniform_optima

Give the optima evenly spaced values by rank?

sigma_mean, sigma_sd

Mean and standard deviation of the normal distribution (truncated at zero) of niche breadths.

rmax_range

Range of the uniform distribution of maximum growth rates.

sigma_signal, rmax_signal

Should niche breadth or maximum growth rate carry phylogenetic signal (Brownian motion)?

optima, sigma, r_max

Optional values of each trait, named by species or in the order of the species, as a vector or a one-column matrix or data frame. They replace the values drawn for that trait.

rescale_optima

Rescale external optima to optima_range?

nodes

Also give the optima at the internal nodes of the tree, as trait_bm() does? They are drawn after all other values, so the traits are the same as with nodes = FALSE and the same seed, and rescaled as the optima of the tips, so they may fall outside optima_range. Not available with external optima or uniform_optima.

Value

Data frame with columns optimum, sigma and r_max, one row per species, with species names as row names. With a tree, the attribute tree holds it, and with nodes = TRUE the attribute nodes holds the optima at its internal nodes.

Details

Any of the three traits can come from elsewhere instead, such as optima simulated by mvMORPH or measured in the field, through optima, sigma and r_max. The other traits are still drawn, and with the same seed they are the same as without the external ones. External optima are rescaled to optima_range, or ranked with uniform_optima, unless rescale_optima = FALSE.

See also

Other species traits: arrival_ages(), as_herodotools(), food_web_rates(), history_rates(), paint_regimes(), partner_turnover(), plot.rate_matrix(), plot_rates(), plot_traits(), rate_matrix(), region_pool(), tip_history_metrics(), trait_bm(), trait_mk(), trait_ou(), trait_rates(), turnover_rates()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10)
species_traits(tr, lambda = 1, sigma_signal = TRUE)
#>        optimum     sigma    r_max
#> t1   81.014935  5.218499 4.731647
#> t2   87.432733  9.461950 4.460504
#> t3   99.189329 14.179416 6.865221
#> t4  100.000000  8.972123 5.629600
#> t5   54.609559  5.850054 5.928344
#> t6    0.000000  9.406866 4.119184
#> t7   29.662989  6.057100 3.621561
#> t8   38.305851 23.586796 7.956104
#> t9   35.050894 13.876716 5.800960
#> t10   5.656532 21.000254 3.279249
species_traits(5)
#>       optimum      sigma    r_max
#> sp1  29.94562  0.6590237 2.382851
#> sp2 100.00000 12.9144624 4.012925
#> sp3  41.12514  5.5670813 6.342356
#> sp4   0.00000 10.0110535 4.025692
#> sp5  45.81600 10.7434132 5.782485
# optima from another model, here an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
ou <- trait_ou(tr, alpha = 1, theta = 0)
species_traits(tr, optima = ou[, 1])
#>       optimum     sigma    r_max
#> t1   95.73952 20.537509 6.528234
#> t2  100.00000 13.356172 5.722460
#> t3   53.57144 14.947958 3.017461
#> t4   61.74475 11.380527 2.373284
#> t5   29.88675  8.812080 2.654176
#> t6   55.81391 11.976843 4.290298
#> t7   26.41955  1.967868 3.015865
#> t8   55.07890 25.800917 3.791915
#> t9    0.00000 24.978188 3.153257
#> t10  16.88222 12.626455 3.543020
